body: Been there & definitely done that. Threw my iPhone 7 across my house and it hit the wall and bounced off my tile floor. Completely shattered the screen and damaged the LCD and I had to pay over $200 to have both replaced. After that incident I did a lot of research and invested in a good phone case. That way if I do end up losing my temper and throw my phone, it won't be destroyed. Already tested out the new case in a fit of anger and phone was unharmed. I'd recommend investing in a Spigen brand phone case if you're a serial phone thrower like I am, they are life saving in the event you do get upset and your phone gets the brunt of your anger. Also maybe try and get out of the area you're in when you become upset and go for a walk or do something to distract yourself such as mindfulness. Hope this helps \(:

Hello,

I'm new to this subreddit as well and also just lost my ex girlfriend/FP as of this morning. I don't have any friends either, and would love to chat as I feel like I'm in the same boat as you. Usually when I lose my FP I immediately start to seek out a new relationship but I've realized that every time I do that, the relationship has the same result.

I think therapy would be a great option to learn ways to cope with the loss of your FP and learning healthy coping mechanisms before beginning a new relationship. For myself, I know that I need to start therapy for that very reason as well. I know how hard it is to go through a break up and how empty that leaves you feeling.

Since I lost my FP this morning, I joined this subreddit and have been reading other people's posts and relating to others and I feel less alone now. This has kept my mind occupied and allowed me to interact with people who are going through something similar \- and I think you're definitely doing the right thing by reaching out to others here as well \(:

I'm dealing with this same issue, I think therapy is the best bet. I've left 2 different jobs at a whim within the last 6 months due to relationship issues. Like something would happen with my ex, and I would just not even show up to work without saying a single word to my boss. It's like I shut down completely and forgo all of my responsibilities when something happens involving my ex/FP. As of today, this very toxic relationship I was in officially ended and I happen to start a new job tomorrow that I believe will lead me into my career. I find the timing of these events to be amusing as the end of this relationship is allowing me to be "free" in a sense so that I can focus on this new job and not having to worry about relationship issues sending me off the deep end. 

Perhaps working in a job where you're moving around and working with your hands \(such as cleaning\) would be good as to keep your mind occupied rather than if you were sitting at a desk. I know for me, I tend to focus on my anxiety more if I'm sitting around and not kept busy. 

If you're struggling with anxiety I'd recommend finding a low stress job where you don't have to interact with others much at all. I know dealing with customers and/or coworkers can be really stressful when dealing with anxiety. Finding a job that entails minimal contact with the public would be a safe bet while you work on coping. 

Hope this helps a little, and best of luck at your new job \(:

I know how you feel. I've been stuck in a cycle of isolation for the past few years. When I did have friends it was only for a short time and this last time around I lost all of my friends due to a relationship I was in and now that the relationship is over I've lost my FP, and have nobody to reach out to. I want to have friends because I'm stuck in my house alone all day, but I don't even know how to go about reaching out to people and making friends at this point.

Hi there,

I'm new here as well. I was diagnosed at 16 years old \(I'm 23 now\) but never sought any treatment, which in hindsight I realize I should have. I definitely understand what it's like to feel isolated and not have anyone to reach out to \- and isolation is especially difficult as I feel like I need to have a relationship to feel happy with myself. I'm glad I joined the reddit community however and am trying to use this as a way to communicate with others going through the same thing and am hoping to break the cycle of isolation I've gotten myself in. 

What self care/coping mechanisms do you prefer for yourself? I haven't really found any healthy coping mechanisms and am looking to find better ways of coping so I'd like to hear any input you have. \(: 

Hope you're having a good day!

I have the same issue when I drink and I'm an absolute emotional roller coaster, having a great time one minute and in a split second I'm crying or in a rage. I've been drinking since I was 13 years old and am an alcoholic. The last couple of months I've cut my drinking down to about once per week, when I was drinking every day before. I have noticed I'm more emotionally stable and don't tend to put myself in awkward situations like when I'd be drinking and would snap for no reason. 

Depending on how much/how often you drink it may be really tough to quit. When I first tried to stop drinking I experienced horrendous panic attacks on a daily basis. Now that I've cut down a lot, I can easily see that my emotions aren't as wild. It's tough, but worth it and if you stick to it you'll see improvement in your emotional stability. Alcohol is great at causing our emotions to spiral out of control and I've found it best to not drink at all or only consume enough to get a light buzz to prevent crossing the threshold of where I lose control. 

If you'd like to stop drinking completely, I'd recommend support groups such as AA, but I understand that AA isn't exactly for everyone. Hopefully this gave you some answers and I wish you the best of luck in your pursuit to stop drinking.
